hindi: कमारी कन्या है विवाह के पश्चात में पैर छूना बेटा गुरु जी के भी तब छोटी कन्या गुरु जी के भी पैर ना छुए
says: An unmarried girl should not touch feet; only after marriage may she touch even the guru's feet, and a small girl should not touch even the guru's feet.
ambiguity: The sentence runs across two caption chunks ('में' | 'पैर छूना ... तब छोटी कन्या'); 'कमारी' is 'कुमारी'.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: स्त्री की रा तो स्ट्रंग करनी संभाल के रखनी सबसे जरूरी है सारा रा का खेल है
says: A woman's aura has to be kept strong and carefully guarded; that is the most important thing, since the whole matter of feet-touching and energy is a game of aura.
ambiguity: 'रा' is read as 'aura', as in earlier sentences.
classical_check: Silent: aura is not a Jyotish term; it summarises his energy-transfer rules above.

gist: Garbled lines ('रे अंदर सब अंदर है उसकी पूजा भी करनी चाहिए नहीं कर उस हमारे अंदर है') about worshipping something that is inside us; speaker and meaning unclear.

hindi: हमारे सबके अंदर दोनों एनर्जी मैस्क फेमिनिन होनी ही है हम सरवाइव ही नहीं कर सकते अदर वाइज
says: Everyone has both masculine and feminine energy inside; without both we could not survive, so the male-female difference in his feet-touching rules is about proportion, not a complete split.
ambiguity: 'मैस्क फेमिनिन' is 'masculine, feminine'; the link to his earlier rules is implied.
classical_check: Silent: ardhanarishvara (Shiva-Shakti in one body) is the traditional parallel.

hindi: आप पूजा जो कर रहे हैं वह भावना है पूजा करना एक भावना है वह भावना चल रही है उसके कारण से ऐसा हो रहा है
says: The puja you perform is a feeling (bhavna): worship is a feeling, and that running feeling is what produces the result, not the outer act.
ambiguity: Said in answer to the earlier question about online puja, but this sentence does not name it.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: bhava is held central in bhakti texts and in the Gita, though Jyotish remedies also stress correct procedure.

hindi: पूजा में आप घंटी बजाओ किसी धर्म में घंटी बजाते हैं किसी में नहीं बजाते किसी में कोई पंखा हिला रहे हैं किसी में कुछ तो अलग अलग है यह भावना है
says: Rituals differ: some religions ring a bell in worship, some do not, some wave a fan; the outer forms vary but the thing that matters is the same underlying feeling.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: अंग्रेज लोग पितरों की कबर पर ले जाकर फूल रख देते हैं वो श्रद्धांजलि दे रहे पितरों को हमारे नहीं देते
says: Westerners take flowers to their ancestors' graves and pay tribute; he says Indians do not give such regular tribute to ancestors.
ambiguity: A comparison made to show what ancestor-honouring means; 'अंग्रेज' covers Westerners in general.
classical_check: Differs: shraddha and tarpana are classical Indian ancestor rites, so his claim that Indians do not honour ancestors is about common neglect, not the texts.

hindi: हमारे को महीने में एक बार अमावस पर य हाथ जोड़ लेना
says: Remedy for ancestors: once a month on Amavasya (new moon), simply fold your hands to the ancestors; he treats this minimal act as enough for ordinary people.
ambiguity: He does not say what to say or whom to face, and 'य' is likely 'ये' or 'यूं'.
classical_check: Agrees: Amavasya is the traditional tithi for pitri tarpana and shraddha.

hindi: अमावस पितृ लोक चंद्रमा पर है यूं भी कर ले
says: The abode of the ancestors (pitri loka) is on the Moon, which is why Amavasya (the Moon's dark day) is the day for honouring them; even this simple way is enough.
ambiguity: 'यूं भी कर ले' follows the previous sentence's hand-fold remedy, so it means 'do it even this way'.
classical_check: Agrees in part: Puranic texts place the pitrs in or near the Moon's realm and make Amavasya the pitri tithi.

hindi: जो हम कहते हैं अरे पितरों के लिए भैया धुआ बत्ती कर लो साउथ की ओर फेस करके
says: What people normally say is to burn incense and light a lamp for the ancestors facing south; he cites this as the usual ritual and, in the next line, finds it too shallow.
ambiguity: He quotes the common practice rather than endorsing it; the criticism comes in the next sentence.
classical_check: Agrees: south is the direction of Yama and the pitrs, and tarpana is done facing south.

gist: Says we Indians are donkeys and the English are better: they place flowers and take food to their ancestors' resting places.
Says we hardly give anything, and when we do we say give it to the rickshaw man outside the colony, not a stranger, because that would be wasted and he will never be of use.

hindi: हम देते तो है ही नहीं देने की बा प्रेम है हां वो प्रेम है देने की भावना प्रेम है
says: Giving is itself love: the feeling of wanting to give is love, and he says we do not really give at all.
ambiguity: 'देने की बा' is garbled and read as 'देने की बात'.
classical_check: Silent: ties to daan as a remedy but he makes no chart rule here.

gist: Audience banter: if giving is love then love us too and give us something; he replies about how much to loot the house.

hindi: हां मतलब तत्व की तत्व ही है भावना ही तत्व है
says: Feeling (bhavna) is itself the essence (tattva) of everything he has just said about puja, giving and ancestors; the inner feeling is the real substance and the act is secondary.
ambiguity: 'तत्व की तत्व ही है' is garbled; the point that bhavna is tattva is clear.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Audience question left incomplete earlier: a very wealthy businessman eats non-veg and has multiple partners, and the same is asked about another community; how do such people improve their planets when the knowledge is in Sanatan?
Says the businessman has become a headline only because so much money recently came to him, and asks where he was some time ago.

hindi: अरे भाई जब पुण्य का घड़ा चालू होता है तो पैसा भी आता है याशी भी करो
says: When the pot of merit (punya ka ghada) starts running, money comes, even if you also indulge in vices; wealth follows stored merit and not conduct at that moment.
ambiguity: 'याशी' is read as 'अय्याशी' (debauchery or indulgence).
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: purva punya (5th and 9th houses) and a good dasha explain wealth despite conduct; the classical texts say conduct affects later results.

hindi: जब य खत्म होकर फट जाएगा तो पैसे भी गए 400 मिलियन बिलियन भी चले जाएंगे यह सब समय का खेला है
says: When that pot of merit is used up and bursts, the money goes too, even a fortune of 400 billion; it is all a game of time. He gives no date, and the example is illustrative.
ambiguity: 'य' is 'ये' (this, the pot). The dollar figure comes from the audience question about one named businessman; this is a general principle, not a prediction about any person.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: dasha cycles and exhaustion of purva punya cause reversals in classical Jyotish.

gist: Tells people to watch the film on the founding of McDonald's: whose restaurant it really was, who bought it and built the empire, and how he looted the original owner.
Says that man committed sin literally yet built an empire, and asks whether it stayed with him; his answer is that it went. The caption is rough and the claim is not a chart rule.
Garbled lines about a name being made and 'K' being worshipped, and that those who are worshipped are the real ones; too broken to read.
Says worship is often done for ego, and those who are worshipped give only ego back.
Mimics guru-style behaviour: all day touching the guru's feet, having to dance, shouting when talking; calls these ways of corrupting the intellect.
Says nobody touches his feet; people bow because of a tormented feeling inside that wants to bow somewhere, and they bow to whoever is there.
Says everyone wants something; nobody touches anyone's feet without self-interest, it is all selfishness.
Challenges the audience to show anyone who goes to God's temple without any desire; every temple visit is driven by wanting something.
Tail of the temple-going answer: some people get great peace in a place of worship, while one who gets that peace at home does not need to go.
People then say the one who stays home is committing a sin; he says he is not, because that person has already received what the visit would give.
Story of a disciple of the Buddha (name garbled in the caption) who realised the truth sitting at home; the Buddha told the monks staying with him to go and learn from him, and they objected.
The monks replied the Buddha was mad since they did their puja and rules; he sent them anyway; the man was a shravaka who learned by listening and never went to the Buddha, yet he knew.
Banter between audience and speaker: last three questions become last two, the style of dialogue changed, and 'you look different today'.
Audience question: does doing remedies interfere with God's plan? He jokes that they should watch the film The Adjustment Bureau.

hindi: हमारे पास मल्टीपल फ्यूचर्स है मल्टीपल पॉसिबिलिटीज है मल्टीपल प्रारब्ध है
says: Each person has multiple possible futures, multiple possibilities and even multiple prarabdhas (fates) available; the chart does not fix one single path.
ambiguity: 'Multiple prarabdhas' is odd, since prarabdha is usually one stock of karma already ripening. It somewhat contradicts his earlier line that fate cannot be changed.
classical_check: Differs: Parashari tradition treats prarabdha as the fixed portion and says remedies and effort alter only how it is experienced; multiple prarabdhas is his own language.

hindi: मल्टीपल उसके भोग के तरीके हैं हम ए की बजाय बी में जाते हैं
says: The same prarabdha can be lived out (bhoga) in multiple ways; through remedies or choices we move from path A to path B, which is how interference is understood.
ambiguity: 'ए' and 'बी' are the letters A and B used as placeholders for two paths.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical remedies are said to change the manner of enjoying or suffering a karma, not its existence.

gist: Brings up the film Avengers: Endgame (the last Avengers film, in which Iron Man dies), where Doctor Strange searches through possibilities.
In the film Thanos is called Brahma because he can end or change the universe with a snap using the Infinity Stones; the cosmic scale is the point of the analogy.
Doctor Strange changes time through a portal and reports he has seen lakhs of possibilities, with only one in which Thanos can be defeated.
Loses the thread, asks what the question was and notes he has wandered into the film; the question was whether remedies interfere with God's plan and what happens if the plan changes.
In the film none of the lakhs of futures has Thanos dying except one, and for that one their own hero must die.

hindi: यानी कि यस ईश्वर के प्लान में चेंज किया लेकिन हमने प्लान सिर्फ चूज किया ईश्वर के पास तो अनगिनत प्लान थे
says: Yes, one can say we changed God's plan, but we only chose one plan from many; God already had countless plans, so our change was a selection among them.
classical_check: Silent: his own answer to whether remedies interfere with divine will.

hindi: हमारे पास जो लिखा है वही होना है वो इधर से इधर से इधर से हम बस बदल सकते हैं खत्म बस होएगा जरूर
says: What is written for us must happen; we can only change the route by which it arrives, but the end result will certainly come.
ambiguity: 'खत्म बस होएगा जरूर' is read as 'it will certainly finish (come to pass)'; the repeated 'इधर से' is the sense of 'this way or that way'.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: the classical view that prarabdha is certain while its route and intensity can be altered by effort and remedy.

hindi: इसको कैसे समझे अब आंसर क्या मिला कुछ नहीं मिला आंसर यह जो हमने प्लान में चेंज किया ईश्वर के यह भी प्लान में था यह मिला
says: The answer to whether remedies interfere with God's plan is that even our change to the plan was part of the plan; our interference was itself scripted.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Analogy: we choose the best plan like a mobile plan, say the yearly one at Rs 3199 with talk time and a free streaming subscription, though he admits not knowing the exact amount.

hindi: तो हम बेस्ट प्लान चूज करते हैं वो भी प्लान में ही है लेकिन इससे बेटर है कि सरेंडर कर तो डायरेक्ट प आ
says: Choosing the best plan is also inside the plan, but it is better to surrender, because surrender brings you directly to the destination.
ambiguity: 'तो डायरेक्ट प आ' is cut and garbled; read as 'then reach directly'.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: surrender (sharanagati) is the Gita's highest advice, outside Jyotish proper.

hindi: इससे बढ़िया है कि हम चुपचाप शिप में बैठ जाए कैप्टन अपने आप पहुंचाएगा जहा पहुंचाना है वो ज्यादा बेटर जानता है शिप चलाना
says: Better still to sit quietly in the ship and let the captain (God) deliver you where you must go, since he knows better how to steer the ship than the passenger does.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: चूज करने हम छोड़ते नहीं ना
says: But we never give up choosing; humans keep trying to pick their own plan instead of leaving it to the captain.
ambiguity: A short aside; 'चूज करने' is 'choose karne'.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Audience remark that the last two questions are always the best ones; speaker agrees to take the last two.
Audience question: how is pitri dosha identified in a kundali, and where does one look for it?

hindi: पांचवे भाव में यदि कोई भी नेगेटिव प्लेनेट पड़ा है नीच का है खराब है दृष्टि नेगेटिव है उसकी तो पितृ दोष है
says: Pitri dosha is read from the 5th house: if any negative planet sits there, or the planet in it is debilitated or poorly placed, or a negative planet aspects it, the chart has pitri dosha.
cells_derived_method: The 5th house is the house of purva punya and the previous line of the family; the affliction type and sign decide how pitri dosha shows: a debilitated Sun points to the father's line, Saturn to delay and burden, Rahu to confusion and unseen causes.

derived_examples.reading: derived: Sun debilitated in Libra in the 5th (lagna Gemini); father's line weak, authority and children matters affected.
derived: Saturn debilitated in Aries in the 5th (lagna Sagittarius); heavy delay and burden through ancestral karma.
derived: Rahu in Leo (the Sun's sign) in the 5th (lagna Aries); disturbance sitting directly on the sign of the father and ancestors.

ambiguity: 'नेगेटिव प्लेनेट' is not defined; he does not say whether he means natural malefics or the functional malefics of the chart.
classical_check: Partly agrees: later practice also reads pitri dosha from the Sun, the 9th house and its lord afflicted by Rahu or Saturn; affliction to the 5th as pitri shaap on progeny is also described.

hindi: गया जाओ श्राद्ध करो यह हो गई पितृ कृपा तो हो गया काम
says: Remedy for pitri dosha: go to Gaya and perform shraddha; that earns the ancestors' grace and the job is done.
ambiguity: The sentence begins 'इसके लिए' at the end of the previous chunk, so the 'for this' refers to pitri dosha.
classical_check: Agrees: pind-daan and shraddha at Gaya are the standard classical-tradition remedy for ancestral dosha.

hindi: सस्ते में 10 20 हजार में हो जाएगा जाने वाले का खर्चा दान की इच्छा कम में भी हो जाए 5000 में भी करते हैं लोग
says: This remedy is the cheap kind: it costs about Rs 10,000 to 20,000 including the traveller's expense, and with a lower donation intent people do it even for Rs 5,000.
ambiguity: Cost figures are only his rough numbers; 'जाने की इच्छा' at the end is the start of the next thought.
classical_check: Silent: costs are not discussed in classical texts.

hindi: महंगे में करना है तो उस ग्रह के प्लानेट के स्टोस पहनो स्टोस कितने के आएंगे बढ़िया स्टोन लाखों के आएंगे
says: For the expensive route, wear the gemstone of the afflicting planet; good stones cost lakhs, which is the price of the permanent remedy.
ambiguity: 'उस ग्रह के' means the planet causing the dosha; he does not say which planet. 'स्टोस' is 'stones'.
classical_check: Differs in part: classical advice is to wear gems of functional benefics and be cautious about gems for malefics causing the dosha.

gist: Complains that people will not spend that much on themselves: they will not gift themselves anything, not even almonds, and will die leaving only property behind.

Joke: a 60-year-old maid sweeps and mops with no pain while the 30-year-old mistress of the house, who orders her around, has pain; they say the maid has drunk ghee since childhood and her bones still work.
Moral of the joke: we do not give ourselves gifts, and over a small matter we use expensive remedies while elsewhere it happens cheaply; the same situation as the hospital example.

hindi: हॉस्पिटल में जो ऑपरेशन 5 लाख का होता है वो गली के नुक्कड़ प 500 में भी करते हैं करने वाले 4 से पाच लाश निकलते है वहां से 500
says: Analogy for cheap versus costly remedies: an operation that costs Rs 5 lakh in a hospital is also done for Rs 500 at a street corner, but four or five bodies come out of there; a cheap remedy is the street-corner operation, with risk and no proper cure.
ambiguity: The sentence starts at the end of the previous chunk ('यह वही हाल है 4'). Unclear whether he endorses the cheap route or warns against it; the corpses detail reads as a warning.
classical_check: Silent: his own illustration; classical texts do not rank remedies by cost.

gist: Audience question: in the gurudwara one gives donation, dakshina or throws money; should this be done even if planetary conditions are not favourable?

hindi: यह हमारा धर्म स्थान है कुंडली में यह कौन सा घर है यह नौवा घर है नाइंथ हाउस धर्म स्थान यह मंदिर गुरुद्वारा इत्यादि इत्यादि कोई सा भी लगा लो
says: Places of worship are the dharma sthan, which is the 9th house of the kundali; temple, gurudwara or any other can be put in this house.
cells_derived_method: Which worship place and which deity suit a person depends on the sign and planet in the 9th house: the 9th's sign lord shows the tradition that supports him and the planets sitting in it show which worship helps or harms.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 9th in Sagittarius (lagna Aries); Jupiter's own sign, so gurudwara, guru-led and ashram-type worship is naturally supportive.
derived: 9th in Aries (lagna Leo); Mars's sign, so temples of warrior deities such as Hanuman suit; his gurudwara rule is applied through Jupiter and Mars together.
derived: 9th in Capricorn (lagna Taurus); Saturn's sign, pointing to austere, old and plain places of worship, the mosque-or-Saturn idea he mentions next.

ambiguity: '[संगीत]' is background music in the caption. He says 'any one can be put' because the classification by planet follows.
classical_check: Agrees: the 9th house is dharma, temples, pilgrimage and guru in all classical texts.

hindi: गुरुद्वारा है तो बृहस्पति के द्वारा लीड किया गया है
says: The gurudwara belongs to the 9th house and is led by Jupiter; he assigns the gurudwara to Jupiter.
classical_check: Silent on gurudwaras (not in classical texts); agrees that Jupiter is the planet of dharma, guru and teaching.

hindi: मंदिर है तो बृहस्पति मंगल के द्वारा
says: A temple is led by Jupiter together with Mars, so a temple draws on both the guru-principle and the warrior-deity energy.
ambiguity: The caption does not say whether Jupiter and Mars lead together or as alternatives depending on the temple deity.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Jupiter is the dharma planet; Mars rules Hanuman, Kartikeya and fire-deity shrines in the usual remedy mapping.

hindi: शनि है तो शायद मस्जिद लेकर चल ले बुध ले ले मस्जिद ले ले
says: A mosque may be taken as led by Saturn, or alternatively by Mercury; he is unsure which planet to give it and tells the audience to take either.
ambiguity: He hesitates ('शायद', 'ले ले') so the assignment is tentative, and he immediately calls it a detail he will not pursue.
classical_check: Silent: mosques are not mapped in classical Jyotish; Saturn as plainness and discipline and Mercury as the written word are classical significations only.

gist: Says that is a detailed point which he will leave and takes the gurudwara as the working example.

hindi: गुरुद्वारा में यूनिवर्सल हो गया
says: The gurudwara is universal: it is open to everyone and not tied to one deity or tradition, which is why he picks it as the example.
ambiguity: The sentence continues with 'गुरुद्वारे की पहली बात' into the next chunk.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: गुरुद्वारे में ना कोई इष्ट नहीं है सबसे बड़ी फायदे की बात क्या गुरुद्वारे की गुरुद्वारे में कोई भगवान का लफड़ा नहीं है
says: The first and biggest benefit of a gurudwara is that it has no ishta (chosen deity), so there is no god-specific complication; no planetary deity can go wrong for you there.
ambiguity: 'लफड़ा' means hassle or mess; read as 'no deity-specific complications'.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Lead-in: takes an example in which the number 9 is written here on the board (the 9th house) before showing how a wrong deity can hurt.

hindi: बेटा पेपर है सरस्वती माता की पूजा कर लेना व फेल होगा क्योंकि व सत्यानाश कर देगी किस्मत फटेगी बच्चे की सरस्वती की पूजा करने से
says: Example of a harmful worship: if you tell a child with an exam to worship Saraswati and the 9th-house sign is the wrong one for that goddess (the caption mentions Rahu), the child will fail, because the goddess will ruin the result and the child's luck will burst.
ambiguity: The sign number is lost in the caption ('अगर राशि ही न नंबर होती'), and Rahu is mentioned without a clear reason; it is not clear which planet Saraswati stands for here. A fail-in-exam outcome is stated as certain.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not warn that worshipping a deity can harm; they prescribe worship for pacifying a planet.

hindi: अगर यहां पर मान लेते चार नंबर है तो हनुमान की पूजा यदि इस व्यक्ति ने की लड़की ने की तो मंगल ग्रह क्या करेगा
says: If the sign number in the 9th house is 4 (Cancer), where Mars is debilitated, and a girl worships Hanuman, then Mars is activated and works against her; worship of the deity of a weak planet harms instead of helping.
cells_derived_method: Same logic across signs: when the 9th-house sign is one where Mars is strong, Hanuman puja helps; when it is a sign where Mars is weak, it harms.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 9th in Aries (lagna Leo); Mars in his own sign, so Hanuman puja supports the dharma house.
derived: 9th in Capricorn (lagna Taurus); Mars exalted in Capricorn, the strongest case where Hanuman worship pays off.
derived: 9th in Scorpio (lagna Pisces); Mars in his second own sign, so Hanuman puja is again supportive though sharper and more secretive in tone.

ambiguity: 'चार नंबर' is read as sign 4 (Cancer); it could be house 4, but the next sentences and Mars's debilitation in Cancer fit the sign reading. He does not say 'debilitated' himself.
classical_check: Differs: classical remedy practice is to propitiate a weak or afflicted planet's deity, not avoid it; a debilitated Mars is usually pacified by Hanuman, so his rule runs against that.

hindi: मंगल ग्रह के पास सारे प्राइवेट पार्ट है से मथ की डेट है किडनी है
says: Mars holds the private parts, the monthly (menstrual) date and the kidney; he lists these as the body areas under Mars.
ambiguity: 'से मथ की डेट' is read as 'monthly date' (menstruation).
classical_check: Partly agrees: Mars is the classical karaka of blood, menses and reproductive organs; kidneys are normally Venus and Libra, so that item differs.

hindi: खा जाएगा ऑपरेशन होगा साधारण तौर पर बेबी नहीं हो सकता इसके साइड पेन रहेगा मंथ की डेट में रो रो के चिल्लाएगी परेशान होएगी
says: If Mars is wrongly activated, it will damage those organs: surgery, normally no baby, side pain, and crying and distress on the monthly date; recorded as his warning, a health claim and not a diagnosis.
ambiguity: A health-outcome prediction stated as near-certain; flagged as not a diagnosis. The 'if' is the wrong Hanuman worship of the previous sentence.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical texts link a strongly afflicted Mars to surgery and menstrual and reproductive troubles; the worship-causes-it step is his own.

hindi: अब हनुमान एक्टिवेट नहीं कर सकते
says: So in such a chart Hanuman cannot be activated (worshipped); do not invoke the deity of the planet that is weak in the 9th-house sign.
ambiguity: The sentence is split across caption chunks ('कर' | 'सकते'). It is a do-not rule given as a conclusion.
classical_check: Differs: Hanuman worship is the standard remedy for a weak Mars in classical and popular practice.

hindi: ऐसे कुछ गलती से गलती हो गुरुद्वारे में पैसा के आते पैसे की प्रॉब्लम आ गई छोटी सी
says: If a mistake is made at a gurudwara, such as giving money there, the damage is only a small money problem, because the gurudwara has no deity to turn the mistake into a big harm.
ambiguity: The caption 'गुरुद्वारे में काकम' is garbled and left out; the rest is read as an account of a minor money problem after giving money at a gurudwara.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: पैसा जो है ये बुध का परर फॉम
says: Money is the pure form of Mercury; cash and paper currency belong directly to Mercury.
ambiguity: 'परर फॉम' is read as 'pure form'.
classical_check: Partly differs: classically wealth is Jupiter (dhana karaka) with Venus for luxury; Mercury rules trade, accounts and paper, so paper money as Mercury is an extension.

hindi: बुध जो है व कागज है वाणी है यह धर्म स्थान है
says: Mercury means paper and speech; he is stating this while referring to the dharma sthan (the 9th house) where offerings are made.
ambiguity: 'यह धर्म स्थान है' is a pointer to the 9th house on the board, not a Mercury attribute.
classical_check: Agrees: Mercury is classical karaka of speech, writing and paper documents.

hindi: यहां पर 12 नंबर राशि यदि है तो बुध ग्रह होता है
says: If the sign in the 9th house is number 12 (Pisces), Mercury becomes the planet that matters for this worship house, and Mercury is debilitated in Pisces.
cells_derived_method: For other signs in the 9th house the planet that matters changes with the sign lord, and its dignity there decides whether worship helps or harms: Mercury in the 9th's own sign is positive, in Pisces the weakest.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 9th in Virgo (lagna Capricorn); Mercury exalted and own, so Mercury's items and Devi-type worship help the dharma house.
derived: 9th in Gemini (lagna Libra); Mercury in its own sign, so offering Mercury things is supportive.

ambiguity: '12 नंबर राशि' is read as sign 12 (Pisces); that Mercury is debilitated there is not stated by him but fits the logic of the passage.
classical_check: Agrees: Mercury is debilitated in Pisces; the link to the 9th is his own 'worship-house' scheme.

hindi: कागज बुध होता है वायु बुध होता है आपका हरे रंग की चीजें हरी दाल इत्यादि
says: Mercury stands for paper, air (vayu) and green-coloured things such as green dal and similar items.
ambiguity: 'वायु बुध' (air) could be Mercury as the air element, or a loose tag.
classical_check: Partly agrees: green and paper are classical Mercury significations; classically Mercury is earth and air is Saturn in most schemes, so 'air' is not standard.

hindi: अगर आपने बुध की चीजें यहां 12 नंबर लिखा है कुंडली में और धर्म स्थान में दी गुरुद्वारे में दे दी मान लो मंदिर में दे दी कहीं भी दे दी
says: If the chart has sign 12 in the 9th house and you give Mercury's things at a place of worship, in a gurudwara, a temple or anywhere, it harms you, since Mercury is weak there.
ambiguity: The sentence's consequence arrives in the following sentences; this row records the condition.
classical_check: Silent: donating items of a weak planet is usually advised against in some remedy lists (dana only for strong planets), but not stated in this form.

gist: Says our fashion and habit is to give cash in God's name.

hindi: भगवान के नाम पर दे नोट दे नोट वो भी हरे रंग का नोट देते हैं 500 का हमारे को खून क से रुलाएगा वो सिर्फ इसीलिए हम रोएंगे बैठ के कि हाय क्या कर डाला
says: Giving notes in God's name, especially the green Rs 500 note, will make us weep blood when Mercury is weak in the 9th; we will sit and cry 'what have I done', so cash offerings can bring heavy loss.
ambiguity: 'खून क से रुलाएगा' is read as 'will make us cry blood'. The money and green-note details are specific to his Mercury and green mapping; the penalty is stated broadly.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: अब बुध है 12 नंबर देवी बुध देवी होती है दुर्गा
says: Mercury is the goddess (Devi) planet, and the goddess is Durga; in the sign-12 case the Durga worship is Mercury worship.
ambiguity: The sentence mixes the sign-12 setting with the general Devi-Mercury link.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Durga is a common Mercury remedy deity in later remedy lists, while Vishnu is the classical presiding deity of Mercury.

hindi: अब आप दुर्गा का मंदिर में जाते हो पूजा करने या बुद्ध को एक्टिवेट कर रहे हो
says: When you go to a Durga temple to worship, you are really activating Mercury; if that Mercury is weak (sign 12 in the 9th), the visit awakens the harm instead of giving help.
cells_derived_method: A Durga visit is helpful when Mercury is comfortable in the 9th-house sign and harmful when it is weak; the 9th-house sign decides.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 9th in Taurus (lagna Virgo); Mercury is friendly in Venus's sign Taurus, so Durga worship brings moderate benefit and not the harm seen with Pisces.

ambiguity: 'बुद्ध' is a caption slip for 'बुध' (Mercury). The sentence ends with 'इससे अच्छा' in the next row.
classical_check: Differs: Mercury afflictions are classically remedied by worshipping its deity, so avoiding it is his own variation.

gist: Sentence cut off at the end of the batch: 'better than this...'; continues in the next batch.

hindi: नास्तिक बन जाओ
says: Completing the previous batch's 'better than this': it is better to become an atheist (not worship at all) than to worship a deity whose planet is weak in the 9th-house sign, since that worship activates the harm.
ambiguity: The sentence begins with 'इससे अच्छा' at the end of the previous batch; the first word 'नास्तिक' is the only visible part here. It is a rhetorical contrast and not a recommendation to abandon faith.
classical_check: Differs: classical Jyotish never advises avoiding worship; remedies are meant to pacify the weak planet through its deity.

hindi: आपका घुटना बोल जाएगा
says: As a result of wrongly activating the weak planet through worship, your knee will give way; a physical breakdown at the knee is the first consequence he names. Recorded as his claim, not a diagnosis.
ambiguity: He gives no planet or house reason for the knee. 'बोल जाएगा' means 'will give up'.
classical_check: Partly agrees: in the classical body map the knees belong to Capricorn and the 10th house (Saturn); his link to the 9th-house worship activation is his own.

hindi: आपके पिता से कलेश शुरू हो जाएंगे आपका भाग्य रूठ जाएगा डाउन हो जाएगा
says: Another consequence: quarrels with your father begin and your luck turns away and goes down; the 9th house of father and fortune takes the hit when it is wrongly activated.
ambiguity: He does not name the house in this sentence; the 9th is understood from the dharma-sthan discussion before it.
classical_check: Agrees: the 9th house is the classical house of father, fortune and dharma, so trouble with father and fortune fits an afflicted 9th.

gist: Aside: 'what a strange thing this is'.

hindi: और रुपए का तो दान ही नहीं करना चीजों का दान कर दो
says: Do not donate money (rupees) at all in this situation; donate things (goods) instead, so that no paper cash carries the planetary effect.
ambiguity: The 'at all' is stated in the sign-12 setting and may apply only there; he may be generalising to every case in this class.
classical_check: Differs: classical dana lists include gold, money and goods; cash is not excluded, so his ban comes from the money-is-Mercury idea.

hindi: 12 नंबर है पीली चीज का दान दो बृहस्पति का है
says: When the 9th-house sign is number 12 (Pisces), donate yellow things; yellow is Jupiter's and Jupiter rules that sign, so the donation uses the sign's own lord.
cells_derived_method: The item to donate follows the lord of the 9th-house sign and whether that lord is strong; if the sign's lord is itself weak, that colour should be avoided.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 9th in Sagittarius (lagna Aries); Jupiter is in his own sign, so yellow donations strengthen the dharma house.
derived: 9th in Capricorn (lagna Taurus); Jupiter is debilitated in Capricorn, so yellow items would be a poor choice, and black items fit better since the sign's own lord is Saturn.

ambiguity: '12 नंबर है' is sign 12 (Pisces) in the 9th house, continuing the earlier example. In his scheme Pisces has Jupiter or Ketu as lord, and here he takes Jupiter.
classical_check: Agrees: yellow items such as turmeric, gram dal and gold are Jupiter's classical donation items, and Pisces is Jupiter's sign.

hindi: तो आपने ये घर एक्टिवेट कर दिया हो सकता है ये ठीक ही है आपको ये ठीक करना है तबीयत ठीक है यहां दृष्टि देगा यहां दृष्टि यहां दृष्टि यह ठीक हो जाएगा
says: By donating yellow things you activate Jupiter and its house; Jupiter then casts its aspect on three places, and whatever needs fixing, such as health, can get corrected through those aspects.
cells_derived_method: Jupiter aspects the 5th, 7th and 9th houses from where it sits, so the area healed depends on which house Jupiter occupies: from the 9th it falls on the 1st, 3rd and 5th houses.

derived_examples.reading: derived: Jupiter in Pisces in the 9th (lagna Cancer) aspects the 1st (Cancer: body and health), the 3rd (Virgo: effort) and the 5th (Scorpio: intelligence and merit), matching his 'three places' and the health mention.
derived: Jupiter in Sagittarius in the 9th (lagna Aries) aspects the 1st (Aries), the 3rd (Gemini) and the 5th (Leo); the same three-way spread falls on self, effort and children.

ambiguity: The sentence is loosely worded and 'तबीयत ठीक है' may mean 'if health needs fixing' or 'health is fine'. 'यहां दृष्टि' is repeated three times on the board without house numbers, read as Jupiter's three aspects.
classical_check: Agrees: Jupiter's full aspects fall on the 5th, 7th and 9th from itself; the donation-activates-the-planet idea is his.

hindi: शनि के लिए करते हैं आप काली चीज दे देते हैं 12 नंबर का मित्र शनि यह धीरे-धीरे आ जाएगा समझ
says: For Saturn you donate black things; Saturn is a friend of the planet connected with sign 12 (Mercury), so this donation is safe and the benefit comes slowly, which is how Saturn works.
ambiguity: '12 नंबर का मित्र शनि' is unclear: Saturn as a friend of Mercury (the weak planet in sign 12) is the reading used here; it could also mean Saturn friendly with the sign's lord Jupiter, which classically is neutral.
classical_check: Agrees in part: Saturn and Mercury are natural friends and black items are Saturn's classical dana; the slow result is classical for Saturn.

gist: Caveat: if the chart had Saturn written at 12 it would be a different matter, and whether Saturn is working is not the point now; he is only giving the broad outline.

hindi: पर यहां कैश जब तक 12 नंबर लिखा है आप रुपया नहीं दे सकते
says: As long as sign 12 is in the 9th house you cannot give cash (rupees) at a place of worship; cash is barred in this chart.
ambiguity: 'यहां कैश' ties the rule to the worship place under discussion.
classical_check: Silent: his Mercury-is-money mapping.

hindi: बुध बुद्ध एक्टिवेट कर दिया कबाड़ा है यानी पैसा देने से भी नुकसान होगी जिंदगी नर्क हो जाएगी कागज रुपया नहीं दे
says: Giving cash activates the weak Mercury, which is a disaster: even donating money will cause loss and life will turn into hell; so do not give paper rupees.
ambiguity: 'बुद्ध' is a caption slip for 'बुध'. 'जिंदगी नर्क हो जाएगी' is a rhetorical exaggeration, not a precise forecast.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: मतलब माथा टेक के आओ माथा टेकना व गुटका पढ़ना यह तो इतना अच्छा हो जाएगा क्योंकि बृहस्पति ऑन कर रहे हो आप ज्ञान की चीज
says: Instead of money, bow your head and read the gutka (prayer book); that is very good, because it switches on Jupiter, the planet of knowledge, and you also do seva at the gurudwara.
ambiguity: 'गुटका' is the small prayer book of the Sikh tradition; 'ऑन कर रहे हो' means 'you switch on'. The sentence flows into 'you do seva in the gurudwara' in the next words.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: study of scripture and guru-seva are classical Jupiter remedies; the gurudwara setting is his example.

hindi: गुरुद्वारे में आप सेवा कर रहे हैं यह 12 नंबर केतु की राशि है केतु है ही दूसरी दुनिया का देवता
says: Doing seva (service) at the gurudwara suits this case because sign 12 is also Ketu's sign in his scheme, and Ketu is the god of the other world, the unseen realm.
ambiguity: He gives Pisces two lords (Jupiter and Ketu) in his scheme; here he takes the Ketu side. 'दूसरी दुनिया का देवता' (god of the other world) is his phrase for Ketu.
classical_check: Differs: classical Jyotish gives Pisces only to Jupiter; Ketu as lord of Pisces appears in some later schemes, not in Parashari texts.

hindi: सेवा से ही चलता है इसीलिए गुरुद्वारे में कार सेवा बहुत चलती है कर हाथों से सेवा प्रसिद्ध है
says: Ketu works only through seva (selfless service), which is why kar seva, service done with one's own hands, is so common and famous in gurudwaras; the Ketu-type act is service and not cash.
ambiguity: 'सेवा' is the last word of the previous caption chunk; 'कर हाथों से' is read as 'kar (hands) seva'.
classical_check: Silent: Ketu is classically moksha, detachment and renunciation; the seva link is his own.

hindi: वो धर्म इस प्रकार का बना कि व होना ही है ऑटोमेटिक इसलिए लोग अंधा फेंक के आते हैं
says: The gurudwara tradition is built so that the right giving happens on its own, automatically; that is why people can throw offerings blindly and still get the benefit.
ambiguity: 'अंधा फेंक के' is rough and read as 'blindly throw (offerings)'; 'व होना ही है' is unclear and read as 'it has to happen'.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: या 12 नहीं होना चाहिए कोई भी नंबर की राशि हो डिपेंड करता कौन सी उसकी चीज देके आओगे
says: Blind giving works unless the 9th-house sign is 12; whatever the sign number is, the result depends on which planet's item you give at the place of worship.
ambiguity: 'उसकी चीज' (its thing) is read as the item of the planet that suits the 9th-house sign; the opening 'या 12 नहीं होना चाहिए' is an exception clause.
classical_check: Silent: his own working rule for the dharma-house gift.

hindi: गुरुद्वारे में रॉकेट की तरह भाग उठेगा
says: If the right item is given at the gurudwara, fortune will shoot up like a rocket; a correct dharma-house gift gives a quick, large rise.
ambiguity: The subject of 'भाग उठेगा' (what rises) is left out; read as fortune (bhagya).
classical_check: Silent: the strength of the claim is his own.

hindi: जिनकी कुंडली में हमें कुछ समझ नहीं आता स्पष्ट बात डॉक्टर को कई बार मरीज का समझ नहीं आता
says: There are charts in which nothing is clear to the astrologer, just as a doctor often cannot understand a patient's case; he admits that some charts cannot be read with certainty.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: क्योंकि कभी पितरों के दोष से कुछ हो रहा है कभी पापा के कभी नया बच्चा पैदा हुआ उसकी वजह से हो गया कई कारण होते हैं घर में वास्तु में कोई चेंज कर लिया पकड़ में नहीं आ रहा
says: Causes overlap and are hard to isolate: sometimes ancestors' dosha, sometimes the father's matter, sometimes the birth of a new child, or a change made in the house's vastu; so the real cause cannot be caught.
ambiguity: A list of possible causes, not a rule that each applies.
classical_check: Agrees in part: pitri dosha and vastu are accepted causes of trouble in later Jyotish practice; a newborn changing the family's chart is a muhurta-era folk idea.

hindi: तो भाग्य उठाते हैं उसका सबसे पहले मंदिर में या गुरुद्वारे में य देकर आ
says: When the cause cannot be traced, first raise the person's fortune (bhagya) by having him give something at a temple or gurudwara; the 9th-house gift is the first step.
ambiguity: 'य देकर आ' is read as 'give and come back'.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: dana at temples to strengthen the 9th house and fortune is a classical bhagya remedy.

hindi: वो दे के आता है ऑटोमेटिक कुछ सपोर्ट मिल जाता है फिर खोपड़ी में आ भी जाता है यह प्रॉब्लम है
says: After he gives and comes back, he automatically gets some support, and then the real cause of the trouble also comes into the head, becoming clear to the astrologer; the gift helps with diagnosis.
ambiguity: 'खोपड़ी में आ भी जाता है' could mean the astrologer understands the cause or the client gets a clear idea; 'यह प्रॉब्लम है' is unclear.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: इसलिए भाग्य धर्म स्थान की बहुत बड़ी महिमा है वहां देना बहुत बड़ी बात देना है
says: The bhagya or dharma sthan (9th house, place of worship) has a very great importance, so giving there is a very big matter, a more powerful act than giving elsewhere.
classical_check: Agrees: the 9th is the house of bhagya, dharma and punya; dana for it is a classical remedy.

hindi: वो असल में देना क्या है पानी में कुछ फेंक दिया कुएं में कुछ डाल दिया जमीन में दबा दिया ये क्या है अलग-अलग स्थान है
says: What does giving really mean? Throwing something into water, dropping it in a well or burying it in the ground; these are different places where the item is deposited and are forms of giving.
ambiguity: A rhetorical question he answers over the next sentences.
classical_check: Partly agrees: flowing items in water and burying them are common classical-tradition and Lal Kitab remedies.

hindi: आपके हाथ से जो चीज टच हुई है उस ग्रह की पीली नीली काली काली लाल वो आपके हाथ से टच होके वहां जा रही है
says: The item of the planet (yellow, blue, black, red according to the planet) that your hand has touched carries your contact with it when it goes into the water, well or ground, so it is your own touch that transfers the effect.
ambiguity: The colour list is not tied to named planets in this sentence; yellow is Jupiter's, blue and black Saturn's, red Mars's in the usual scheme.
classical_check: Agrees in part: planet colours and offering items by colour are classical dana rules; the touch-transfer idea is his.

hindi: तो हमने उस ग्रह की औरा को वहां गाढा है दबाया है बहाया है वो ग्रह हल्का पड़ जाता है उसको हल्का किया जाता है
says: So the planet's aura has been buried or flowed away there, and the planet becomes lighter; remedies work by lightening the planet's load, not by adding to it.
ambiguity: 'गाढा' is read as 'buried'.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: weakening a malefic's hold through dana and visarjan is a classical idea (pacification).

hindi: यह परहेज की तरह है उपाय इस तरह चलते हैं
says: This is like parhej (dietary abstinence): you cut the planet's load as you would cut a food, and remedies in general work in this way.
ambiguity: The sentence follows directly from the aura-burying sentence, which spills across the caption chunk boundary.
classical_check: Silent: the parhej analogy is his own.

hindi: इसलिए सिर्फ धन दे देने से काम होगा नो नॉट गुड
says: So merely giving money will not do the work; it is not good, because the remedy has to match the planet and the lightening method.
ambiguity: 'काम होगा' is a question: 'will the work be done?', answered 'no, not good'.
classical_check: Differs in part: classical dana accepts money, but proper items by planet are preferred.

hindi: 12 नंबर यहां बैठा है यह बच्चा है आपका बच्चे को कभी भी कैश मत देना आपसे दुश्मनी करेगा
says: If sign 12 sits in the house that represents your child (the 5th), never give the child cash, because he will turn against you; the weak-Mercury cash rule applies to money given to children too.
cells_derived_method: Cash given to a child is harmful only when the sign in the child's house makes Mercury weak; in signs where Mercury is strong, money gifts to the child are not a problem.

derived_examples.reading: derived: 5th in Virgo (lagna Taurus); Mercury is exalted and own, so cash gifts to the child are safe and even supportive.
derived: 5th in Gemini (lagna Aquarius); Mercury in its own sign, so there is no cash ban.

ambiguity: The house on the board is called 'यह बच्चा है आपका' without a number; the 5th (children) is read here. The weak Mercury in sign 12 follows the earlier logic and is not restated.
classical_check: Agrees in part: the 5th is the classical house of children; a Mercury-based cash ban is his own.

hindi: उसे दारू पीनी पड़ेगी याशी करेगा खराबी करेगा लड़ाई झगड़ा करेगा
says: The child who is given cash in that case will have to drink liquor, indulge in vices, spoil himself and fight and quarrel; the cash feeds Rahu-type and Mercury-weakness habits in the child.
ambiguity: A behavioural prediction about a child, recorded as his claim and not as a certainty. 'याशी' is read as 'अय्याशी'.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: यह बहुत बड़ा लफड़ा है यह बहुत बहुत बड़ी खिचड़ी है यह इंडिविजुअलिस्टिक है बहुत ज्यादा
says: The whole matter of what to give, where and to whom is a big mess and a big khichdi (mixture); it is highly individual, so no single remedy fits everyone.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: classical texts also say remedies must be chosen per the chart and person.

gist: Closing remarks: that is the story for now, there will be many more questions to take later, the programme will continue, and he ends today's class.
Thanks to everyone for joining and coming, greetings and namaste, and says it is his good fortune that people are learning something through him.
Sign-off: see you again next week; music begins.
